newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Competition body studies Portugal tobacco sale.
newsitem.headline: Competition body studies Portugal tobacco sale.

text.p: Portugal's Economy Ministry has referred the coming privatisation of state tobacco firm Tabaqueira to the country's competition watchdog for an opinion on the impact on the local market, a ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
The spokesman said that the newly-formed Competition Council, which only formally takes office next Monday, would have 30 days to study the case.

The candidates to buy Tabaqueira are the U.S. group Philip Morris, in partnership with Portugal's Jorge de Mello group; state-owned Spanish tobacco company Tabacalera, allied to Madeira company Empresa Madeirense de Tabacos; and French group Seita.

Although the only official target date for the sale of a 65 percent stake in Tabaqueira is the end of the year, government officials had said previously that they hoped the sale would be wrapped up in early November.

The Economy Ministry, which is responsible for the state's industrial holdings, had decided to seek the opinion of the Competition Council because whoever won the bidding would clearly dominate the local tobacco market, the spokesman said.
Tabaqueira accounts for 70 percent of Portuguese cigarette sales.
"It is a delicate issue and we want to avoid any doubts," the spokesman said, even if the opinion of the competition watchdog was not binding on the government.
"The final decision rests with the cabinet on the recommendation of the Finance Ministry," he said.

The government's special privatisation jury, which is used to evaluate bids in cases where the state is not simply floating a stake on the market, ranked the Philip Morris offer first, ahead of Seita and Tabacalera.

The U.S. firm did not offer the highest price for the tobacco concern, whose sale is expected to bring in over $200 million. But the jury's decision, which is also not binding, took account of the candidates' plans for developing the industry.
